clips.title: Npm workspaces tutorial
clips.why: You see one workspace depend on another and import its code by package name, which is exactly how the broker imports shared.
look: How the internal dependency is added to the package.json of the package that uses it.
The import uses the package name, not a relative path into the other folder.
Nothing is published: npm links the folder.
clips.after: In ai-agents the broker and the orchestrator depend on @rhinohealth/ai-agents-shared the same way, and both import RunScope from it.

clips.title: What Is A Monorepo And Why You Should Care - Monorepo vs. Polyrepo
clips.why: The 'easier refactoring' argument is the heart of this lesson: in one repo, a change and every caller it breaks can land in one pull request.
look: Why a change across separate repos needs several pull requests that must be released in the right order.
In one repo, the change and its callers are reviewed together.
The cost he mentions: everyone shares one CI, which is why our root scripts run every workspace.
clips.after: That is the RunScope rename: in ai-agents it fails the root typecheck in every service that uses the field, inside the pull request that made it.

practice.q: Complete the broker's import so it uses the shared workspace by its package name.
practice.why: Workspaces are imported by package name. npm's link in node_modules turns that name into the shared folder.

practice.q: After npm install at the root, what is node_modules/@rhinohealth/ai-agents-shared?

options.text: A link to the shared folder
options.why: npm links each workspace by its name, so edits in shared are seen at once.

options.text: A copy of shared made at install time
options.why: A copy would go stale after your next edit. Workspaces use links.

options.text: A package downloaded from the npm registry
options.why: Nothing is published or downloaded under that name. The root package is private.

practice.q: Complete the root script that runs the typecheck of every package.
practice.hint: The flag that means 'in every workspace'.
practice.why: --workspaces runs the script in each workspace in list order, and --if-present skips the ones without that script.

practice.q: You must rename a field of RunScope. Put the steps of a safe change in order.
items: Run npm run typecheck at the root
Fix each error it reports, in every workspace that uses the field
Run npm test, which builds shared first and runs every workspace's tests
Open one pull request that holds the rename and all the fixes
practice.why: The rename happens in one place, the root command finds every consumer, and one pull request keeps the pair of services in step.
